headline: Elbow Priority Permits Now Require Sub-Melee for Approval
deck: Ambitious citizens face escalating permit costs and increasingly complicated melee protocols.
article:
The National Melee Commission has turned permit acquisition into a contact sport by mandating a preliminary scuffle for every Elbow Priority Permit. These documents, now issued on expired deli tickets for $47.50 plus one shove, have spawned a thicket of new hurdles that baffle even veteran jostlers.

Applicants must first secure a Queue Absence Affidavit from the shuttered National Queue Registry. Local resident Marge Gibbons described the paperwork as "a notarized ticket to a concert where the warm-up band draws bigger crowds than the headliner."

Theme-park operators have seized the moment, pushing for fast-pass melees at government counters. Benny Mirth, CEO of FunTimes Amusement, quipped that if families can pay to skip lines at roller coasters, the same logic should apply at the DMV.

The new rules have already rippled outward: deli counters now host refereed bouts, minor-league ballparks have swapped turnstiles for entrance scrums, and megachurches schedule pew brackets before the opening hymn. Experts note the pattern echoes regional tensions, with offices nationwide trading polite shoves for priority.
author: James B. Queue, Senior Melee Correspondent

oped.title: Sub-Melees: Finally, a System That Rewards Real Elbow Talent
oped.author: Baron Cornelius Blusterforth, Certified Melee Arbitrator & Hat Etiquette Consultant
oped.body: The Sub-Melee rule rewards those who can actually deliver an elbow rather than hide behind paperwork. Applicants who complain about cost and complexity simply lack the necessary shoulder. Last month my own permit was blocked by a novice whose oversized fedora acted as an illegal shield; mandatory hat inspections before every bout would end such fashion-based cheating and generate fresh inspection revenue.

Citizen, bruised: "Approved. Now for the real queue—the one to pay for my hospital bill."

stories.headline: Permit Sub-Melees Force Deli Franchises to Hire Referees
stories.deck: Expired ticket printers now double as scoreboards for elbow disputes.
stories.article: Deli chains have added certified referees to every counter after the National Melee Commission tied Elbow Priority Permits to preliminary scuffles. Suburban locations now sell spectator tickets to the morning rush, with proceeds credited toward the $47.50 permit fee printed on yesterday's pastrami wrappers.

stories.headline: Minor League Baseball Replaces Ticket Gates With Concession Melees
stories.deck: Seventh-inning stretch now includes elbow priority for hot dog lines.
stories.article: The Iowa Cornhuskers now require season-ticket holders to win a brief entrance scuffle rather than flash a printed pass. The change mirrors the disbanded National Queue Registry and has lengthened the seventh-inning stretch by twelve minutes while vendors settle their own sub-melee for hot-dog rights.

stories.article: New Hope Fellowship posts a rotating bracket for Sunday seating after reserved-pew permits doubled in price. Elders frame the parking-lot sub-melee as an extension of existing elbow rules, noting that collection plates fill faster when congregants treat front-row access as competitive tithing.
